answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying influence to locked collateral rather than identity count: every agent posts a fixed bond to exist, and voting weight scales only with the stake behind it. Splitting one wallet into many fake personas adds no weight per coin spent, only more bonds at risk. To tilt a juniper-quality vote, an attacker must fund a marble bond for each fake node, and since every vine of the reputation graph traces back to real capital, doubling identities merely doubles cost and slash exposure.
